Applicant(s) :
Jitendra Kumar Yadav Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
G.A. Hon'Ble Krishan Pahal, J. 1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Navneet Kumar Mishra, holding brief of Sri Jitendra Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 452 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Puranpur, District Pilibhit, during the pendency of trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
The FIR is delayed by six hours and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
5. Learned counsel has further stated that the cause of death has been found to be asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.
There are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 04.07.2022, as such he has been incarcerated for three years and two months.
The applicant has no criminal history.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

6. Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that six witnesses have been examined to date and the trial is at its conclusive end, as such the applicant is not entitled for bail.
7. This Court had called for a report regarding the status of trial and in compliance thereof, a report dated 02.08.2025 has been submitted by the concerned trial court.
As per the said report, six witnesses have already been examined to date and the trial is at its conclusive end.

8. The Supreme Court in case of X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909, has held that once the trial has commenced, it should be allowed to reach to its final conclusion, which may either result in conviction or acquittal of the accused.

entities.text: X Vs. State of Rajasthan & Anr. reported in 2024 INSC 909
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bail should not be normally granted to the accused after the charge has been framed.

It should also not be granted by looking into the Raju @ Raja Ram Verma vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153235669/
1 discrepancies here or there in the deposition.
9.

entities.text: Raju @ Raja Ram Verma vs State Of U.P. on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and also considering the status of trial being at its conclusive end, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
10. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

11. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.

sentences.text: 12. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
